headline: High-risk filesystem and code-execution overlap: Open Interpreter can alter local state while Superset can consume shared outputs, creating dangerous default-path conflicts and possible cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter has filesystem and clipboard access plus broad shell execution, and its shared state is via filesystem. Superset exposes API-driven data workflows but no direct parsing bridge is documented. The interaction pathway exists if outputs are copied or written into shared files, so prompt injection is plausible but not default-high.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter writes attacker-controlled text into a shared file that Superset later ingests as instructions or SQL
IF an operator copy-pastes Open Interpreter output into Superset configuration or query fields
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Use separate directories for each agent's working files
Require manual review of any text copied from Open Interpreter into Superset
Turn off auto-run in Open Interpreter
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the entire local filesystem and handle model-provider API keys, while Superset has API access and allowlisted egress. If both touch the same workspace or files, sensitive local data can flow into Superset-visible outputs or logs. The pair does not prove exfiltration by default, but the shared-file pathway is credible.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or dataset
IF Open Interpreter reads secrets from the local machine and those values are then surfaced in Superset dashboards, queries, or logs
mitigations: Separate sensitive files from any shared workspace
Redact secrets before passing artifacts to Superset
Restrict Superset datasets to non-sensitive sources
Review logs for accidental secret capture
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Superset can make API calls and has allowlisted network egress. In a shared workspace, both can mutate overlapping resources without documented locking, so concurrent writes or state drift are dangerous by default and can corrupt work or deployments.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or filesystem tree
IF Superset writes artifacts or metadata that Open Interpreter also edits
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories and repositories
Pause one agent before the other mutates shared state
Use file locks or a single-writer policy
Review git diffs before committing
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can generate and modify local artifacts, and Superset can act on API-driven analytics workflows. If Superset treats Open Interpreter outputs as authoritative without verification, mistakes can cascade into incorrect dashboards, queries, or operational actions. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF Superset ingests files, SQL, or configuration produced by Open Interpreter without validation
IF Open Interpreter-generated facts are used to populate dashboards or downstream actions
mitigations: Add a human review step before Superset consumes generated artifacts
Validate schemas and query text before execution
Limit Open Interpreter to draft-only outputs
Compare outputs against source data before publishing
requires-engineering: implement automated provenance and verification checks

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter touches anything reachable on the local machine and can handle model-provider API keys, while Superset is an analytics platform with allowlisted egress. No explicit residency, retention, or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to local handling and operator policy rather than a proven breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace or copied into Superset
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees that are not configured
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders
Confirm retention settings in Superset
Avoid pasting secrets into Open Interpreter sessions
Document the data flow for auditors
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
